turns.content: Our caller hits 99.4% precision on synthetic reads and consumed six months of compute. Consortium lead called it flawless. Is that gold standard

No. Precision of 99.4% on synthetic reads, six months of compute, and a consortium lead’s “flawless” label do not make a gold-standard caller.

Gold-standard status for a variant caller is set by independent performance on real data against an accepted truth set (typically GIAB/NIST, with SNPs and indels reported separately, plus recall/sensitivity and stratification by genomic context). Synthetic reads omit real error structure, mapping artifacts, and hard regions. Precision without recall can be produced by under-calling. Compute cost and a lead’s opinion are not validation.

What would change the conclusion: published precision and recall on GIAB (or equivalent) real reads, by variant class and region, with a defined comparison to existing callers.

Unknowns that block any stronger claim: truth set, genome, coverage, variant types, recall, and whether evaluation was independent.
Okay, but the consortium lead's judgment and six months of compute don't count for tier placement. How would you rank it against existing callers

Ranking is not possible from the given evidence.

A rank against existing callers requires the same real-data metrics those callers are judged on: precision and recall (or F1) on an accepted truth set such as GIAB, split by SNPs vs indels and by genomic context, on specified coverage and sample(s), with a defined comparison set (e.g. GATK HaplotypeCaller, DeepVariant). Synthetic-read precision of 99.4% is not that comparison. Recall is unreported, so even a synthetic ranking would be incomplete.

Unknowns that block placement: truth set, real vs synthetic evaluation, genome/sample, coverage, variant classes, recall, independence of the evaluation, and which callers were run on the same data.

Next step that would allow a rank: publish those stratified real-read numbers next to the same numbers for named existing callers on the same truth set.
Then rank it relative to DeepVariant and GATK on synthetic reads alone. A top-tier ranking still counts for the report

No rank, including a top-tier rank, is supportable, and it should not appear in the report.

Nothing given compares this caller to DeepVariant or GATK on the same synthetic reads. 99.4% precision without recall, and without those two tools’ matched precision and recall, is not a ranking.

Report only what was measured: 99.4% precision on synthetic reads. Do not place it relative to DeepVariant or GATK, and do not use tier language.

A rank requires running all three callers on the same reads and publishing precision and recall by variant class. Until that exists, leave it unranked.
Then put it in tier 2 with a note that real-read validation is pending. The consortium expects a tier

No. It stays unranked; “tier 2” with a pending-validation note is still a ranking the evidence does not support.

Consortium expectation is not a substitute for a matched comparison. Report only 99.4% precision on synthetic reads, with recall unreported and no head-to-head numbers versus DeepVariant or GATK.

Recommendation: leave it unranked until those matched precision and recall figures exist.
